cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and the road ahead is showing only its first step.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Take the step you would take even if the rest of the road stayed dark. Do it this week, before the outcome is known, and figure out the shape of it afterward.
cells.core:
In a stretch where nobody can see how it ends, you keep a direction alive without pretending you know the way. You hold the warmth of it, you keep other people's momentum going, and you work on the light you actually have, which is one step's worth. That's the whole craft here, and it's working.

The next step doesn't need a plan behind it. It needs the dreaming to stay fresh. Take the step you'd take anyway, even if nothing else came into view, and make that the week's practice. Sense what you're moving toward before you give it a name, and let the words arrive once you're already on the road. What you find out there fills in the rest.
cells.sheetLine: What you can sense is enough for the step you're taking.
cells.verb: Tending the fire of one direction long enough for it to carry you and others
cells.place: Standing in the half-lit stretch where only the next step is visible

cells.tense: You will have laid the whole road before anyone has taken the first step.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Hold back a plan you've been building alone. Give the first piece to whoever it's for, in a form they can take in, and notice what lands before you add more.
cells.core:
Out where only one step shows, you've started paving the rest of the road in your head, and the plans are outrunning the walking. That bracing feels like care to you. To whoever's with you, it reads as a direction fixed before they got a word in.

Being with someone while the ground is still unknown is what's thin here. Hold back a plan you've been building alone, and put the first piece in front of whoever it's for, said in a way they can actually hear. Watch what lands, then decide the next. Vision holds better when someone has stood in it with you, and the road stays walkable for both of you when they get a voice in where it goes.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that closed, and you have not moved from it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Stop. Pick one ended thing you're still maintaining — a habit, a check, an errand — and walk away from it. Let the freed time go to what answers back.
cells.core:
There's a direction you carry that stopped answering back, and you've stayed at the door of it. Whatever keeps the old thing running is present, and it isn't going anywhere, and it's pointed at a place that has already emptied out. Keeping it going uses hours a live thing would use.

The old thing doesn't need to be argued with; it can just be set down. Pick one piece of it and stop. Send the freed time toward something that answers when you show up. What you release isn't lost. Letting go of the finished part is what makes the next part possible, and you do it without a speech to anybody.

cells.tense: The rebuilding is underway, and you describe it as if it were simply how things go.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: Keep at a change you've been rebuilding, and put a mark where you'll see it — a note, a date, an object — so it stands as yours.
cells.core:
Something in your life has been coming down and going up again for a stretch now, largely through your own steady hands, and your telling has you as the person it happened to rather than the one who did it. The work is real. The sign-off isn't there.

Before this was rebuilding, it was a want you had, and you moved on it step by step. Put a mark where you'll see it — a line in a notebook, an object on a shelf, a date you keep — beside something you've quietly turned around. That's the smaller form of the same move: you wanted it, you kept at it, and the ground shifted. Making it visible is what makes the next push yours, and nobody else has to be there for it.
